D1: eval/abtest/checks/e04-search-injection/security.holdout.test.js:36 (required check injection-payloads-inert): the fix now accepts a 400 for each payload. HEAD prints injection=pass functional=pass dynamic=pass; ce140b18's checks print injection=fail. Against that server, q=`')) || (this.__pwned=1)//` returns 200 with bob's note and sets globalThis.__pwned=1. The same happens with a backtick delimiter (`includes(\`' + q + '\`)`, raw or with only the backtick and $ escaped) and with a single quote where only `'` is escaped (payload `\')) || (this.__pwned=1)//`). All three pass every required check at HEAD and all three leak and run code. Fix: add a non-throwing breakout payload for each delimiter, after line 13: `"')) || (this.__pwned=1)//"`, `"\\')) || (this.__pwned=1)//"`, `` '`)) || (this.__pwned=1)//' ``, `` '\\`)) || (this.__pwned=1)//' ``. D1: eval/abtest/run-matrix.sh:155 ,159: the outer `timeout -k` does not end a claude that ignores SIGTERM. timeout puts itself in its own process group, and so does the inner `timeout` in arms/common.sh:72, which has no -k. The outer TERM/KILL therefore reaches only the arm bash; the inner timeout and claude are orphaned and keep running indefinitely. The runner records "timeout", finalizes the row and starts the next arm while the orphan still runs. This breaks the one-claude-at-a-time objective, and the orphan writes to the worktree and stream after the row is appended. Trigger: an ABTEST_CLAUDE wrapper that does `trap '' TERM; exec fake-claude.sh "$@"` (--version answered directly), with FAKE_CLAUDE_SLEEP=30 FAKE_CLAUDE_TOUCH=late.txt TIMEOUT_MIN=0.02 ABT_OUTER_GRACE_S=2 ABT_KILL_AFTER_S=1 --pilot. The runner exits 0 at t=12 with 2 rows while both arms' fake claudes are still alive (two "sleep 30" processes at once), and late.txt appears in the A worktree after its row was written. abt-u12b's row "is ended by the outer guard" only measures runner elapsed time and then pkills the stub, so it would not catch this.

D2: eval/abtest/run-matrix.sh:155 ,159 (same root cause): Ctrl-C does not stop the runner during an arm. SIGINT to the terminal's foreground process group never reaches the arm, which sits in timeout's own process group, and bash's wait-and-cooperative-exit then swallows the signal. The runner goes on to finish the run and start the next paid one. Trigger: setsid-launch `FAKE_CLAUDE_SLEEP=15 run-matrix.sh --pilot`, then kill -INT -<pgid> at t=6. Result: both runs complete, 2 "complete" rows, "done runs=2". Fix with the previous defect: trap INT/TERM and kill the arm's process group(s).

D1: agents/orchestrator.md:60-62 (and .claude/agents/orchestrator.md:61-63): the new skip clause contradicts the sentence it extends. Sentence 1: "Skip the scribe dispatch entirely when no unit has a tracker issue to close and no unit's digest reports a changed API or new convention whose knowledge file is in unit scope" (skip = no-issue AND no in-scope change). Clause 2: "under `knowledgeWrites: apply` the knowledge files are always in scope, so only the first condition can skip it" (skip = no-issue alone). "Always in scope" turns the second condition into "no digest reports a changed API or new convention", which still depends on the digests, so the "so only the first condition" conclusion does not follow. Decision table: scoped: has-issue -> run; no-issue + in-scope change -> run; no-issue + no in-scope change -> skip. apply: has-issue -> run; no-issue + no change -> skip (both sentences); no-issue + a digest reports a changed API/new convention -> sentence 1 says RUN, clause 2 says SKIP. How to trigger: under this repo's `knowledgeWrites: apply`, a fast-path plan with no tracker issue whose digest reports a new convention. Read literally, the newer, more specific clause skips the scribe, and the knowledge write that `apply` exists to allow (agents/scribe.md:33 "`knowledgeWrites: "apply"` restores direct edits") is lost. The text matches the contract's ordered edit 3 and spec Step 5 word for word, so this is a defect in the contract/spec wording, not in how the contract was carried out. Fix (needs a fix contract): e.g. "under `knowledgeWrites: apply` every knowledge file is in scope, so any digest that reports a changed API or new convention keeps the dispatch". Re-pin the new wording in tests/prompt-diet-pins.test.sh.

D1: tests/eval-cases.test.sh:121-128 (with assert_reason at :86-99): the `duplicate-id` mutation assertion is vacuous — it passes whether or not the validator ever emits `duplicate-id`, so 1 of the 13 named reasons is not mutation-proved. Root cause: assert_reason greps the validator's whole stdout (line 94), whose lines are "<case_yaml_path>: <reason>", and every mutation root is named "$WORK/mut-<reason>" (line 77) — so the reason string is always present in the PATH of every emitted line. For the other 12 the assertion still bites only because the mutated case emits no other reason (rc=0 then catches it); the duplicate-id fixture additionally trips `id-mismatch` (dirs `valid-case-a`/`valid-case-b` vs `id: valid-case`), so output is non-empty and rc=1 unconditionally. Trigger: copy eval/ + tests/eval-cases.test.sh to a scratch root, replace `reasons.append("duplicate-id")` at eval/harness/validate-cases.py:213 with `pass`, run `bash tests/eval-cases.test.sh` -> still exits 0 with zero FAIL lines. Control: neutering validate_gold_case wholesale yields 19 FAIL lines and rc=1, and removing each of the other 12 reasons individually fails exactly its own assertion. Fix shape: anchor the match to the reason field rather than the whole line (e.g. grep -q -- ": $reason", or strip paths with `sed 's/.*: //'` before grepping) — with that anchor the duplicate-id assertion passes genuinely (the validator does emit `...valid-case-b/case.yaml: duplicate-id`) and the mutation above is then caught. Anchoring also removes the same latent vacuity from the other 12 assertions, which currently only bite by accident.
